Hi, I'm James Lindsay (jimbo).

I'm the Director of Software Engineering and a bioinformatics engineer in the Department of Data Science at the [Dana-Farber Cancer Institute](https://www.dana-farber.org/).

My work sits at the intersection of cancer genomics, spatial biology, and clinical informatics. I spend my days building software and data infrastructure that translates massive genomic datasets into something clinicians can actually use to help patients.

Most notably, I helped architect **MatchMiner**, an open-source platform that automatically matches cancer patients to clinical trials based on their genomic profiles. I also led the development of **ImmunoProfile**, a machine-learning workflow that uses spatial data to understand the tumor immune microenvironment.

I've also built infrastructure for major national consortia like **AACR Project GENIE** and contribute to the **cBioPortal**.
